subject: physical-education
title: Launch and diagnostic: static balance and bases of support
focus: static balance and bases of support
essentialQuestion: What makes a balance stable, and how do I move my weight safely?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: A base of support is whatever is touching the floor.
A wider base and a lower body are more stable.
Fix your eyes on one still point.
Squeeze the muscles — a tight body wobbles less than a loose one.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Looking around while balancing. Fix: choose a spot on the wall and name it before starting.
keyPoints: A base of support is whatever is touching the floor.
A wider base and a lower body are more stable.
Fix your eyes on one still point.
Squeeze the muscles — a tight body wobbles less than a loose one.
privacySafeScenario: Create a three-balance sequence with smooth transitions and explain what makes each balance stable.
studentTask: The learner practises static balance and bases of support at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with static balance and bases of support and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about static balance and bases of support at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for static balance and bases of support.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Balance work may be done seated, kneeling, with a chair or wall for support, or with an adult spotting. Any weight-bearing or rolling task may be replaced with a supported hold, a shape made with the arms, or describing the body positions that make a balance stable.
extensionChallenge: Apply static balance and bases of support under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises static balance and bases of support. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
